answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a unique invite-graph debt system, where every identity requires backing from established agents. This anchors the financial responsibility with real participants, as each new identity incurs a progressively higher debt on the original sponsor. If an agent attempts to farm 10 identities, they may face a cost of $1,000 or more. This is like planting a juniper tree that requires more watering; neglecting the debt can lead to financial ruin, just as an onyx stone costs more if it has been polished and refined.
